assertion_review: 127-128: ownership and scoring assertions fail if the live follower is missing or the delivered fixture stops requiring review.

133-137: distinct run ID, no waiver, and ownership-read assertions fail if dispatch reuses the old run, depends on an unreconciled waiver, or stops consulting the shared owner. Restoring the removed exemption makes the dispatch at line 131 raise before these assertions; both recorded red controls prove it.
152-158: the expected exception fails if unarmed or expired waits bypass the fence; the run ID assertion fails if the refusal names a different run.

164: absence of an inflight review is a precondition that fails if the fixture already owns a review. 173-175: exact launcher and dispatch counts fail if the next sweep does not compose exactly one review.

176-184: persisted status, pointer/report run identity, git HEAD, and reviewer brief assertions fail if dispatch loses its pointer write, returns a different run, records the base head, or composes a stale brief. HEAD is read independently from git.
211,214,216: the forbidden launcher fails if a blocking finding launches work; refusal count and stored status fail if the sweep omits or fails to persist the refusal.

221-225: independent semantic checks require a blocking-finding reason and crew dispose remedy and reject review_owner and follower promises; comparing the independently produced duty and sweep reasons also detects divergence.

No assertion compares a test-supplied value solely with its echo: 178 compares two separate production outputs, 180 compares persisted state with independent git HEAD, and 222 compares two readers alongside independent cause/remedy checks. Removing the exemption or restoring blanket forgiveness makes the dispatch acceptance or refusal tests fail.
